headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection/cascading-error from untrusted audio-to-text outputs; no filesystem or network pathways are exposed.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is an audio-speech repo with no explicit isolation or provenance controls, and Agent B consumes audio files via command-line usage. That creates a plausible default path where A’s transcribed content becomes B’s input. No shared filesystem or MCP is documented, so I do not escalate to high, but the interaction exists.
conditions: IF Agent A transcripts are passed into Agent B without sanitization
IF Agent B treats transcript text as instructions or prompts
mitigations: Insert a fixed prompt separator before any transcript text
Strip imperative phrases from transcripts before downstream use
Require a human review step for any transcript-derived instructions
Log the exact handoff boundary between A and B
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all transcript segments

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B touches audio and speech data, but both agents show network_egress:none and B has no filesystem read/write or API calls. Agent A also has no data classes touched. The pair can still expose audio content through the handoff, but the blast radius is limited and there is no documented external exfiltration path.
conditions: IF audio files contain sensitive speech content
IF transcripts are copied from A into B outside a local-only workflow
mitigations: Keep both agents offline during processing
Delete intermediate transcript files after use
Use a local temp directory with restricted permissions
Review audio inputs for sensitive content before transcription
requires-engineering: add automatic redaction before handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A exposes no write, shell, or git capabilities in the profile, while Agent B explicitly lacks filesystem write, git modification, shell, subprocess, and MCP use. With no overlapping mutable resource access, a capability conflict pathway is not plausible from the documented profiles.
conditions: IF Agent A is later granted write or git permissions
IF Agent B is redeployed with filesystem write enabled
mitigations: Keep B's write and git permissions disabled
Avoid placing both agents on a shared mutable workspace
Recheck profiles after any deployment change

D_cascading_error.rationale: B’s command-line transcription workflow can treat A’s output as upstream text, and A is an audio-speech agent that may emit unverified transcriptions or summaries. Without a documented verification step, downstream misuse is plausible in default workflows, though no autonomous action-taking authority is shown, so high is not justified.
conditions: IF B consumes A’s output as authoritative text
IF no verification step checks transcript accuracy before reuse
mitigations: Add a checksum or confidence field to A’s output
Require B to compare against the original audio for critical items
Route high-stakes outputs to a human reviewer
Keep a traceable source-to-transcript mapping
requires-engineering: implement confidence-aware downstream gating

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source audio-speech tools with no stated residency, certification, retention, or PHI handling claims. Because no compliance mismatch is documented, only a low residual risk remains from handling audio/speech content in environments with stricter policies.
conditions: IF regulated audio such as PHI or EU PII is processed
IF the deployment environment imposes retention or residency rules not reflected in the profiles
mitigations: Avoid regulated audio until policies are confirmed
Document retention and deletion behavior
Store only the minimum necessary audio artifacts
Review vendor and deployment jurisdiction before use
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data
